exercise_36.answer: Currents in resistive windings dissipate energy as thermal energy. Changing flux also induces circulating currents in the conducting core, producing resistive heating. Insulated thin laminations interrupt large interlaminar current loops and reduce eddy-current loss; they do not eliminate every loss mechanism.
exercise_36.scope: Do not require hysteresis or assert eddy currents always dominate total loss. Unlike a heat engine, an ideal transformer does not require rejection of heat as part of its energy conversion.
